channel.title: Japan AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Japan's political, economic and security developments

item.title: Storm menaces Japan after highest cyclone tally since 1966
item.description: Tropical Storm Surigae is currently 791 kilometers south-southeast of Okinawa, packing top sustained winds of 74 kilometers per hour.

item.title: Japan growth minister says economy has exited reflationary phase
item.description: Minoru Kiuchi's comments follow renewed weakness in the yen and further gains in government bond yields this week.

item.title: Asian Games off to chaotic start as doubts grow over Japan’s ability to host
item.description: Problems from playing the wrong national anthem to accommodation issues have cast a cloud over the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.

item.title: Japan’s newest party gets off to rocky start with zero percent support rate
item.description: Media polls showed the support rate for the Democratic Reform Party, formed last week with 18 members, is at zero percent.

item.title: The Japan Times Prep School Fair set for Oct. 24; registration now open
item.description: The Japan Times, Ltd. (Head office: Chiyoda Ward, Tokyo; Chairperson and Publisher: Minako Suematsu) will hold The Japan Times Prep School Fair, bringing together boarding schools and international schools from Japan and overseas, in Akasaka, Tokyo, on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. Registration for the event is now open.

item.title: The Japan Times プレップスクールフェア
item.description: 株式会社ジャパンタイムズ（本社：東京都千代田区、代表取締役会長兼社長：末松弥奈子）は、国内外の名門ボーディングスクールやインターナショナルスクール参加する「The Japan Times Prep School Fair」を、2026年10月24日（土）に東京・赤坂で開催します。現在、来場登録を開始しました。

item.title: Trump shared concerns over weak yen with Takaichi
item.description: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said she would continue to coordinate with her U.S. counterpart Scott Bessent.

item.title: LDP panel calls for permit system for key land acquisitions
item.description: In the draft, the team also pushed for a ban on individuals working for foreign governments from acquiring land deemed critical to national security.

item.title: Swiss franc, Japanese yen Rise as DeepSeek News Boosts Safe Havens
item.description: The Yen and Swiss Franc were stronger against the dollar as investors sought safe havens after Chinese start-up DeepSeek’s new AI model hit U.S. tech stocks.
